Job Title:
Business Operations Analyst - Cancer Prevention and Survivorship

Department:
CCC | Sponsored Research

Position Summary

The Business Operations Analyst 2 provides comprehensive operational, programmatic, and administrative support for the Center for Cancer Prevention and Survivorship (CCPS). This position serves as a key coordinator supporting center leadership, faculty investigators, research staff, trainees, community partners, advisory committees, and institutional stakeholders. The individual is responsible for coordinating business operations, supporting strategic initiatives, managing center activities, monitoring performance metrics, facilitating communications, and assisting with the implementation of programs that advance the center's research, education, outreach, and survivorship missions.

The position works closely with the Administrative Director, faculty leadership, and affiliated research programs to ensure effective coordination of center activities, compliance with reporting requirements, efficient business operations, and achievement of strategic goals. The Business Operations Analyst 2 serves as a central resource for project coordination, committee management, reporting, communications, event planning, and operational support across a diverse portfolio of cancer prevention and survivorship initiatives.

Job Duties

Program Operations and Strategic Initiative Support

- Coordinate day-to-day operational activities for the Center for Cancer Prevention and Survivorship.

- Support implementation of strategic plans, center priorities, and institutional initiatives.

- Develop and maintain project plans, timelines, work plans, and implementation schedules for center activities.

- Monitor progress toward strategic goals and facilitate follow-up on deliverables and action items.

- Coordinate activities involving multiple faculty, departments, colleges, and external organizations.

- Identify opportunities for process improvement and assist in implementing operational efficiencies.

- Support special projects and initiatives as assigned by center leadership.

Leadership, Governance, and Committee Coordination

- Coordinate activities of center leadership teams, working groups, committees, and advisory boards.

- Develop meeting agendas, briefing materials, presentations, and supporting documentation.

- Attend meetings, prepare minutes, track decisions, and monitor completion of action items.

- Coordinate logistics for executive meetings, retreats, strategic planning sessions, and advisory board meetings.

- Maintain committee records and governance documentation.

- Provide administrative and logistical support to center leadership and affiliated faculty.

Data Management, Reporting, and Business Analytics

- Develop and maintain databases tracking faculty participation, grants, publications, trainees, partnerships, presentations, and center activities.

- Collect, verify, analyze, and summarize data for annual reports, progress reports, strategic planning efforts, and institutional requests.

- Prepare dashboards, metrics reports, and performance summaries for leadership review.

- Monitor key performance indicators related to research productivity, funding, outreach, education, and survivorship programs.

- Assist with preparation of materials supporting Cancer Center Support Grant (CCSG) reporting and other institutional reporting requirements.

Research and Faculty Support

- Support coordination of shared center resources, faculty initiatives, pilot projects, and interdisciplinary research activities.

- Assist with tracking grant applications, funded projects, publications, and collaborative activities.

- Coordinate information gathering for grant proposals, center applications, and program evaluations.

- Support faculty recruitment activities including interview coordination, candidate visit planning, presentations, and stakeholder engagement.

- Assist with onboarding activities for new faculty and staff affiliated with the center.

Events, Educational Programs, and Outreach Activities

- Coordinate seminars, workshops, conferences, symposiums, survivorship programs, and community engagement activities.

- Manage registrations, event communications, catering, facilities, audiovisual needs, and vendor coordination.

- Prepare event materials, promotional content, evaluation tools, and post-event reports.

- Support outreach initiatives involving community organizations, healthcare partners, and advocacy groups.

Communications and Stakeholder Engagement

- Coordinate internal and external communications on behalf of the center.

- Assist with preparation of newsletters, announcements, website content, reports, fact sheets, and promotional materials.

- Maintain center calendars, distribution lists, and communication platforms.

- Disseminate information regarding funding opportunities, center activities, achievements, and events.

- Serve as a point of contact for faculty, staff, trainees, community partners, and institutional stakeholders.

Administrative and Financial Support

- Assist with procurement requests, travel coordination, and business transactions.

- Monitor operational expenditures and assist with budget tracking.

- Coordinate purchasing, reimbursements, and financial documentation in accordance with university policies.

- Support record retention and compliance activities.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business administration, public administration, health administration, communications, higher education administration, public health, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Two or more years of experience coordinating programs, projects, business operations, or administrative functions. Demonstrated experience managing multiple priorities and deadlines. Experience preparing reports, presentations, and business documentation. Strong organizational, analytical, and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in an academic medical center, cancer center, university, or healthcare setting. Knowledge of cancer prevention, survivorship, public health, clinical research, or population sciences. Experience supporting faculty, research programs, grant-funded initiatives, or interdisciplinary centers. Experience coordinating committees, advisory boards, workshops, conferences, or strategic planning activities. Experience with reporting systems, dashboards, and performance metrics. Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Teams, SharePoint, project management platforms, and database management systems.

Job Title:
Assistant Clinical-Track Faculty: Business Analytics

Department:
Fisher College | Operations and Business Analytics

The Department of Operations and Business Analytics (OBA) within Fisher College of Business, at The Ohio State University, invites applications for a Clinical-Track faculty position specializing in Business Analytics (Assistant Rank). This will be a full-time appointment, to begin Autumn semester 2027. The salary is competitive with leading research universities.

We seek candidates who are committed to excellence in teaching and curriculum development in business analytics and artificial intelligence. The successful candidate will develop and teach courses for undergraduate, graduate, and executive education students, with responsibilities that include curriculum and syllabus design and the development of course content and instructional materials. The candidate will also contribute through service and leadership activities that support the educational and outreach missions of Fisher College of Business.

While teaching and curriculum development are the primary performance objectives for this clinical-track position, the successful candidate will also be expected to generate impactful scholarly output that advances the college’s educational and/or outreach missions. Such contributions may include research, practitioner-oriented writing, teaching cases, textbooks, classroom simulations, and other innovative pedagogical materials.

Immigration/visa sponsorship may be available in very limited situations (e.g., F1/OPT to H-1b, H-1b change of employer), but all decisions concerning immigration/visa sponsorship will depend on an evaluation of complexity and risk.

Performance Objectives:

Principal tasks will include: curriculum and syllabus design, content and materials development, teaching, and service and leadership activities in support of the missions of the college. The selected candidate will be expected to complete activities and provide support for developing and teaching undergraduate, graduate, and executive education students within the domain of business analytics/AI. While excellence in teaching and curriculum development are the primary performance objectives, clinical assistant professors at Fisher are also expected to generate impactful scholarly output within the domain of business analytics that furthers the educational and/or the outreach missions of the college (e.g., through research, writings geared toward practitioners, teaching cases, textbooks, classroom simulations, and other forms of innovative pedagogical materials).

Education and Experience Requirements:

Minimum requirements for the position are a terminal degree (PhD, DBA, or equivalent) in a business or related field, completed by the start date of employment.

Candidates ideally would have an established record of excellence in knowledge dissemination within the domain of business analytics/AI, but we will also consider newly graduating candidates with clear potential to develop such a record. Similarly, candidates ideally would have an established record of effective related service (e.g., curriculum development and program management), but we will also consider candidates with clear potential to do so.

Desired attributes for ideal candidates include the flexibility to teach courses across business analytics and operations management; significant practical business experience within the field of business analytics and, potentially, operations management; experience in teaching executive education; and a strong record of service and outreach with the business community. It is also desired that the candidates have already, or have the potential to, create scholarly output as described above.

Additional Information:

Assistant Clinical Professors in this department currently have a base salary of $150,000-$175,000. The offer for this position will be based on internal equity and the candidate's qualifications.

Ohio State provides access to a depth and breadth of opportunities and resources. Starting your first day, Ohio State offers you a comprehensive benefits package.

The College:

Fisher College of Business has a rich research tradition and engages through the college and the Graduate School in programs at the undergraduate, master and doctoral levels. The nationally ranked Fisher College of Business is one of 15 colleges within the university, with approximately 9,000 undergraduate and 1,200 graduate students.

Department Information:

The mission of the Department of Operations and Business Analytics is to provide world-class research, teaching, and outreach in operations management, purchasing, supply chain management, and business analytics. The department is committed to advancing scholarship, practice, and public policy, while delivering innovative educational experiences across its undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral programs.

The University:

Ohio State is a top-20 public university, and its Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is one of America’s leading academic health centers. Eligible Ohio State employees receive comprehensive benefits packages, including medical, dental and vision insurance, tuition assistance for employees and their dependents, and state or alternative retirement options with competitive employer contributions.

Grounded in Ohio State University’s Shared Values, our university community welcomes differences, encourages open-minded exploration and courageous thinking, and upholds freedom of expression.

Ohio State is a dynamic community where opportunity thrives, and individuals transform themselves and their world. Positions are available in countless fields and specialties. Become a Buckeye and contribute to an incredible legacy that serves to guide our future and shape a better tomorrow.

The Ohio State University is committed to enhancing academic excellence. Recruiting, supporting, and retaining faculty of the highest caliber is a core component of this commitment. The Office of Academic Affairs (OAA) has established central resources to focus on offering support to new and prospective faculty and their loved ones. Service offerings include dual career partner consultation, potential employer and/or employment opportunity identification, consultation and resources related to relocation, as well as identifying opportunities to engage on campus and in the surrounding community. While employment opportunities are not guaranteed, resources and consultation are available. More information about dual career and faculty recruitment can be found here.

In addition to being responsive to dual-career opportunities, we strongly promote work-life balance to support our community members through a suite of institutionalized policies. Ohio State is a member of the Michigan, Ohio, Western Pennsylvania & West Virginia HERC.

Located in Ohio’s capital city, Ohio State’s Columbus campus is near the center of a rapidly growing and vibrant metropolitan area with a population of over 1.5 million. jobs.description:
Position Title:
Professor of Information Systems and Business Analytics (ISBA)

Appointment Type:
Faculty

Job Description:

Summary of Duties and Responsibilities:

The Department of Information Systems and Business Analytics (ISBA) in the Ivy College of Business at Iowa State University invites applications for a tenured position at the rank of Professor. The position includes an endowed chair for a distinguished candidate with an exceptional record of research excellence and leadership in Information Systems and Business Analytics.

The position holder will demonstrate the ability to maintain an active, high-quality research program that contributes to leading journals in MIS and related fields, demonstrate effectiveness in teaching, provide leadership in advancing the department's research and academic reputation, and fulfill normal service expectations.

This is a full-time, 9-month appointment beginning August 16, 2027. A later start date may also be considered. Initial review of applications will begin on September 30, 2026, but applications will continue to be accepted until the position is filled.

The position holder will conduct high-impact scholarly research suitable for publication in leading MIS journals such as Information Systems Research, Management Information Systems Quarterly, and The Journal of Management Information Systems. The holder will also be expected to contribute to mentoring Ph.D. students, and teaching ISBA-related courses at the Ph.D. level, as well as undergraduate or Master's levels.

In addition, the position holder is expected to play a key role in advancing the department's research reputation through collaboration, mentorship, and leadership, helping to further enhance the department's national and international standing in ISBA research and education.

The appointment also carries the expectation of typical institutional and professional service for the rank of Professor.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis without sponsorship. Immigration sponsorship is not available for this position.

Required Minimum Qualifications:

-
Ph.D. in MIS or a closely related field

-
An outstanding record of scholarship, eligible for a tenured position at Iowa State University

-
An established and active record of publishing research in top-tier IS journals such as Information Systems Research, Management Information Systems Quarterly, and The Journal of Management Information Systems.

Preferred Qualifications:

-
An influential scholarly reputation, as evidenced by scholarly citations and service to the profession

-
An active research pipeline, including papers targeted or invited for revision at premier journals

-
Experience in mentoring junior faculty and doctoral students

-
Experience as a full-time, tenure track or tenured faculty member

-
A record of effective teaching of ISBA-related courses

Department/Program & College Description:

The Ivy College of Business at Iowa State University, established in 1984, furthers Iowa State University’s land-grant ideals by training students to be knowledgeable and ethical communicators, leaders, collaborators, and problem solvers through impactful research, innovative teaching, and community engagement.

With the largest undergraduate business program in the state of Iowa and nationally ranked graduate programs, the Ivy College of Business is home to over 5000 students with a strong growth trajectory. We pride ourselves on our high ethical standards and our drive to promote an environment where all individuals may succeed academically, professionally, and personally. Each member of our community is committed to the college’s mission to link theory with practice for tomorrow’s business leaders.

The college offers undergraduate, graduate, and Ph.D. programs and is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International). Less than five percent of business schools worldwide receive this accreditation.

The faculty in the Department of Information Systems and Business Analytics are active in their field. They have published in premier journals such as Information Systems Research, MIS Quarterly, Journal of Management Information Systems, Management Science, the Journal of the Association for Information Systems, and Decision Sciences Journal. They serve or have served as editors, associate editors, and members of editorial boards for leading information systems journals. ISBA faculty have received doctorates from premier programs such as Arizona, Carnegie Mellon, Indiana, Northwestern University, and UT Dallas. ISBA faculty have active research projects in business analytics, cybersecurity, healthcare, IT strategy, artificial intelligence, and other IS and analytic areas. Ph.D. students graduating from the ISBA department have been placed at schools such as Notre Dame, Alabama, Oklahoma, Oklahoma State, Mississippi State, University of Cincinnati, and Florida Atlantic University.

This is a part-time position at 50% FTE, averaging approximately 20 hours per week, with flexibility in scheduling work hours.

What You’ll Do

- Analyze operational data to identify trends in sample volumes, testing activities, customer service, turnaround times, revenue, workload distribution, and program performance.

- Develop recurring and ad hoc reports, dashboards, visualizations, and performance metrics to support decision-making and operational improvements.

- Collect, organize, clean, validate, and maintain data from multiple systems to ensure accuracy, consistency, and completeness.

- Investigate data discrepancies, resolve reporting issues, and collaborate with information technology staff on system updates and improvements.

- Maintain documentation of data definitions, reporting methods, business rules, and data quality standards.

- Support accreditation reviews, annual reporting, program assessment, and evaluation of organizational goals and performance measures.

- Participate in user testing and validation of system updates and reporting modifications.

- Help staff access, interpret, and use reports and data resources; develop training materials and user documentation as needed.

- Follow established data governance practices and FAIR data principles to ensure data is findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable.

- Provide basic support for reporting systems and business applications and assist student employees or project participants as assigned.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience analyzing data to identify trends, patterns, or operational performance measures.

- Experience developing reports, dashboards, or data visualizations using Excel, Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools.

- Experience collecting, cleaning, validating, and maintaining datasets from multiple sources.

- Experience using databases, reporting systems, or business applications to retrieve, organize, or manage data.

- Experience documenting data definitions, reporting procedures, or data quality standards.

- Experience communicating analytical findings or providing training and technical assistance to help others use data and reporting tools.

- MS SQL and MS Visual Studio experience.

Why Join Us?

The Seed Science Center is a preeminent institution in American agriculture with a longstanding history of supporting the seed industry through research, education, testing, and outreach. You'll join a close-knit team of approximately 30 employees who value collaboration, build strong working relationships, and create a welcoming environment. This is an opportunity to contribute to meaningful work while becoming part of a team that takes pride in its work and enjoys connecting through shared activities.

About the Opportunity

The candidate will be hired as a Data Analyst I.

This is a term position that may have an opportunity for renewal.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis without sponsorship. Immigration sponsorship is not available for this position.

Position Title:
Assistant Professor: Technology - Urban Analytics and Planning

Appointment Type:

Job Description:

Summary of Duties and Responsibilities:

The Department of Urban Planning and Development (UPD) in the College of Design at Iowa State University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in technology, urban analytics and planning. We seek a scholar and educator whose research and teaching connect data and emerging technologies to contemporary urban and regional issues. The successful candidate will strengthen the department’s capacity in planning methods while developing a forward-looking research agenda that explores how emerging technologies can enhance the ways planners understand, analyze, visualize, and shape places. This work should demonstrate careful attention to the ethical and responsible use of data and technology in planning research and practice.

Areas of Interest

This position provides an opportunity to strengthen and modernize core departmental capacity in planning methods while building new strength in AI, urban analytics, visualization, and using technology in planning. Areas of research and teaching interest may include: urban analytics and data-driven planning, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies in planning, PlanTech and digital planning tools, quantitative planning methods, data visualization and geovisualization, emerging issues in technology and planning, and ethical and responsible applications of AI and data in planning. The position is intended to connect analytical and technological innovation with planning practice.

Position Responsibilities

The successful candidate will be expected to:

- Develop and maintain a nationally recognized program of research and scholarship, including pursuing external funding appropriate to the defined research agenda.

- Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in planning methods, urban analytics, technology in planning, and/or related areas. Contribute to other planning courses, studios, and other departmental curricular needs. Integrate emerging technologies and contemporary analytical methods into planning education. Mentor undergraduate and graduate students and serve on graduate thesis committees.

- Collaborate with faculty across the College of Design, ISU Extension and other units at Iowa State University.

- Contribute to departmental, college, university, and professional service.

In addition, faculty in UPD have an opportunity to work with ISU Extension and Outreach, Community and Economic Development, during the summer.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis without sponsorship. Immigration sponsorship is not available for this position.

Required Minimum Qualifications:

Ph.D. degree in urban and regional planning, community and regional planning, geography, urban studies, or a closely related field by the time of appointment.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Evidence of potential for effective undergraduate and graduate teaching.

- Research and teaching expertise in two or more of the following: urban analytics, AI and emerging planning technologies, quantitative methods, and data visualization.

- Evidence of potential to develop a strong program of research and scholarship and secure external research funding.

- Experience with interdisciplinary, applied, or community-engaged research.

- Experience integrating emerging technologies into teaching and/or professional planning practice.

Department/Program & College Description:

About Department of Urban Planning and Development

The Department of Urban Planning and Development (UPD) at Iowa State University prepares students to address the complex challenges facing cities, towns, and regions. Through teaching, research, and community engagement, UPD faculty focus on areas such as land-use planning, housing, transportation, community and economic development, environmental resilience, local governance and planning technologies, with a strong emphasis on applying planning knowledge to real-world community needs. jobs.description:
Georgetown University comprises two unique campuses in the nation’s capital. With the Hilltop Campus located in the heart of the historic Georgetown neighborhood, and the Capitol Campus, just minutes from the U.S. Capitol and U.S. Supreme Court, Georgetown University offers rigorous academic programs, a global perspective, and unparalleled opportunities to engage with Washington, D.C. Our community is a close-knit group of remarkable individuals driven by intellectual inquiry, a commitment to social justice, and a shared dedication to making a difference in the world.

Requirements

Job Overview

The Research Data Coordinator 1 position is responsible for data management for phase I, II, and III oncology clinical trials conducted within the Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center Clinical Trials Office (CTO) of the Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center (LCCC).

Additional duties include, but are not limited to:

-
Supports all aspects of clinical research data management for clinical trials conducted in the Lombardi CTO, including collection of data from source documents and medical records and completion of case report forms per sponsor requirements.

-
Supports trials of varying complexity and disease indication.

-
Works collaboratively with trial stakeholders and internal study teams (physicians, Regulatory team, Study Coordinators, nursing staff, Research Laboratory Technicians, and Research Pharmacy team).

-
Reviews and analyzes information from medical records (clinic notes, pathology reports, radiology reports, patient questionnaires, etc.) to extract data for all assigned research protocols - including but not limited to industry, national, and investigator-initiated studies.

-
Accurately captures data in electronic or paper Case Report Forms (eCRFs/CRFs), adhering to contractual timelines and site Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

-
Ensures query resolution with proper physician and clinical study team oversight within site- and sponsor-specific time requirements.

-
Requests and uploads radiological images into sponsor-provided imaging platforms according to each study protocol.

-
Resolves imaging-related queries with the assistance of clinical study team.

-
Collects and organizes source documents in electronic and paper format according to site policies.

-
Ensures accuracy of data entered in the Clinical Trials Management System (CTMS) with patient information and key dates.

-
Interfaces with study team members to resolve discrepancies.

-
Schedules sponsor monitoring and study close-out visits.

-
Provides support during internal and external monitoring and auditing preparation, including supporting data deficiency corrections and development of corrective actions plans post-audit.

-
Communicates appropriately with pharmaceutical sponsors, study monitors, auditors, physicians, and study team members.

-
Collaborates closely with physicians and Study Coordinators to maintain protocol integrity.

-
Attends protocol-related training and completes all required study training in the required timeframe.

-
Prepares for - and participates in - site initiation visits.

-
Assures ongoing compliance with all departmental, institutional, and federal requirements and regulations.

-
Maintains controls to assure accuracy, completeness, and confidentiality of research data.

-
Maintains confidentiality standards for all potential and enrolled study participants; and complies with federal Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) regulations.

-
Performs all duties in accordance with all applicable laws and regulations.

-
Adheres to Georgetown University Medical Center’s philosophies, policies, and SOPs.

-
Works in compliance with Human Subject Protection regulations, patient confidentiality/HIPAA requirements, and Good Clinical Practice.

-
Other duties as assigned.

Work Interactions

Clinical Research Manager

-
Disease Group members: Principal Investigators, Physicians, Clinicians

-
Lombardi CTO members: Clinical Research Nurses, Clinical Research Coordinators, Data Coordinators, Regulatory Coordinators, Laboratory Technicians

-
External department clinicians and staff: Infusion Nurses, Oncology Pharmacists, hospital staff

-
Clinical trial sponsors, auditors, and study monitors

Requirements and Qualifications

-
High School Diploma or GED required.

-
Up to two (2) years of related experience required.

-
Strong candidates exhibit:

-
Ability to work independently and function within a team.

-
Strong attention to detail.

Reliable and able to prioritize competing responsibilities.

jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.description:
What We Do:

Data Scientists at the SEI use advanced statistics, data analytics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to help our government and industry clients research and solve cybersecurity challenges. In this role, you will work with our customers to identify areas where advanced statistical techniques can help tackle problems, plan and develop prototype solutions, and build out final products. You'll get a chance to work with elite cybersecurity professionals and university faculty to build new technologies that will influence national cybersecurity strategy for decades to come. You will co-author research proposals, execute studies, and present findings to DoW sponsors and at academic conferences.

Our team works on a wide range of projects. Our current work includes research in generative AI and large language models, computer vision, multimodal AI, agentic AI, and assurance of AI systems. Additionally, we craft metrics and experimental designs for large-scale cybersecurity research programs, develop human-in-the-loop machine learning solutions, and build classifiers to identify security vulnerabilities. If you are a data science or statistics expert with an interest in cybersecurity, we want to hear from you!

Requirements:

- BS in data science, machine learning, computer science, statistics, or related highly-quantitative discipline with eight (8) years of experience or equivalent combination of training or experience; or MS in data science, machine learning, computer science, statistics, or related highly-quantitative discipline with five (5) years of experience; or PhD in data science, machine learning, computer science, statistics, or related highly-quantitative discipline with two (2) years of experience.

- Willingness to complete modest travel to various locations to support the SEI’s overall mission.

- You will be subject to a background check and must be able obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of War security clearance.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

- Experience in predictive modeling, data science, and/or AI & machine learning

- Deep understanding of statistical modeling techniques and advanced data analytics

- Proficient with at least one mathematical/statistical programming package (e.g., R, python numpy/scipy/pandas/polars, MATLAB, etc.)

- Innovative and inquisitive with ability to imagine novel analytical solutions to problems Thrives in a multi-disciplinary environment

- Strong communication skills

- Expertise in one or more of the following:

- Recommendation systems

- Time-series forecasting (Prophet, NeuralProphet, Chronos, Lag-Llama, etc.)

- NLP / LLMs (fine-tuning, RAG, evaluation, prompt engineering)

- Causal inference / uplift modeling / synthetic controls

- Modern ML frameworks: LightGBM/XGBoost, CatBoost, PyTorch,JAX, TensorFlow)

- LLMs / agentic workflows (LangChain/LlamaIndex/Haystack)

- Experience deploying models (FastAPI, Triton, KServe, SageMaker, Vertex AI, or similar)

- Experience working with big data (Spark, Trino, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks)

Desired Experience:

- Experience in cybersecurity and privacy is a plus is a plus

- Experience in U.S. Government work and/or with FFRDCs, UARCs an National Labs is a plus

- Demonstrated ability to learn new concepts and grow into new areas of work

Joining the CMU team opens the door to an array of exceptional benefits.

Benefits eligible employees enjoy a wide array of benefits including comprehensive medical, prescription, dental, and vision insurance as well as a generous retirement savings program with employer contributions. Unlock your potential with tuition benefits, take well-deserved breaks with ample paid time off and observed holidays, and rest easy with life and accidental death and disability insurance.

Additional perks include a free Pittsburgh Regional Transit bus pass, access to our Family Concierge Team to help navigate childcare needs, fitness center access, and much more!

For a comprehensive overview of the benefits available, explore our Benefits page.

At Carnegie Mellon, we value the whole package when extending offers of employment. Beyond credentials, we evaluate the role and responsibilities, your valuable work experience, and the knowledge gained through education and training. We appreciate your unique skills and the perspective you bring. Your journey with us is about more than just a job; it’s about finding the perfect fit for your professional growth and personal aspirations.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

Brown University Athletics and Recreation is seeking candidates for the Athletics Business Analyst position. Located in Providence, Rhode Island, and a member of the Ivy League, our intercollegiate athletics program consists of 38 varsity teams with approximately 1,000 athletes who participate within the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA-DI).

The Athletics Business Analyst provides financial transaction support, independent budget analysis, forecasting, reconciliation, and financial guidance for an assigned portfolio within Brown University Athletics and Recreation. The position reviews and resolves complex financial issues, interprets spending trends and commitments, prepares actionable financial reports, and develops recommendations that support informed resource planning by coaches, unit leaders, and Business Office leadership. The Analyst exercises judgment within established University procedures and delegated responsibilities, while escalating material risks, exceptions, and decisions concerning budget allocations or operational policy to appropriate leadership.

Education and Experience

- Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business administration or a related field and 3–5 years of relevant financial analysis, budgeting or accounting experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

- Experience in higher education or athletics financial operations preferred.

Job Competencies

Indicate the essential job competencies. Competencies are required knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to perform the job successfully.

- Demonstrated ability to analyze financial data, explain variances and develop reliable forecasts and actionable recommendations.

- Knowledge of accounting principles, financial controls, reconciliation and transaction documentation.

- Strong spreadsheet, financial reporting and data analysis skills; familiarity with Workday or comparable enterprise financial systems preferred.

- Ability to research and resolve complex financial discrepancies independently and exercise sound judgment about escalation.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to advise nonfinancial stakeholders clearly.

- Excellent organization, accuracy, discretion and ability to manage competing deadlines.

All division employees are required to demonstrate exemplary ethical conduct and conformance to NCAA rules and regulations; the duties of the position are to be performed in compliance with all NCAA, Ivy League rules and regulations; and any rules violations on behalf of themselves or any knowledge of violations within the division are to be reported to the compliance office and appropriate parties.

Employees in coaching positions must receive annual rules education on NCAA legislation related to recruiting by the compliance office and maintain current AED/CPR and First Aid certification (certification is available at no cost through the Division).

jobs.title: Associate Consultant - Entry-Level Technology Consulting
jobs.description:
Veeva’s Consultant Development Program (CDP) is an accelerated pathway that transforms early-career professionals into high-impact consultants who deliver cloud and AI solutions, helping global Life Sciences companies bring life-changing therapies to patients. 
 
The Role
You’ll work hands-on with innovative technology, collaborating directly with internal teams and external customers, implementing our products to solve complex business challenges. In this role, you’ll learn our industry-leading cloud platforms and work with cutting-edge AI solutions to transform how life sciences companies operate. Empowered from day one by a team-first culture, you will accelerate your career growth as a technical consultant who thrives in an environment where we work hard for our customers and each other. 
Start Date: July 2027

The Program
As part of the Consultant Development Program, you will:

- Ramp up quickly. Your journey begins with an intensive, team-based onboarding program that combines hands-on learning, transparent feedback, and active collaboration to develop the consulting skills and industry knowledge to make an impact right away.

- Learn by doing. You won't be watching from the sidelines. You will take on real responsibility and work directly with customers to solve problems within your first three months.

- Thrive together. Grow alongside a supportive team of seasoned leaders and peers who actively champion your development through open communication and actionable feedback.

- Build your future. Advance from Associate to Consultant in less than 2 years. More importantly, you’ll develop the foundation for a successful, long-term career where you can continually expand your technical expertise, lead complex projects, and evolve with our global and diverse team.

What You'll Do
As part of our Professional Services team, you are a strategic partner guiding customers through implementation. We will teach you how our software works, and you will use that knowledge to design, configure, and deliver solutions that drive real business value. Your day-to-day will involve:

The Payment Integrity DRG Coding & Clinical Validation Analyst position has an extensive background in acute facility-based clinical documentation, and/or inpatient coding and has a high level of understanding of the current MS-DRG, and APR-DRG payment systems. This position is responsible for reviewing medical records for appropriate provider documentation to support the principal diagnosis, co-morbidities, complications, secondary diagnosis, surgical procedures, POA indicators to validate coding and DRG assignment accuracy, insuring the physician documentation supports the hospital coded data.

The Commercial Analyst I is part of our global Commercial Finance team and supports cross-functional processes, stakeholders, and timelines to ensure customer contract proposals, budgets, and contract modifications are completed accurately and efficiently throughout the contract lifecycle.

- Finalize customer-facing financial and contractual documents after obtaining required internal approvals, performing quality control reviews to ensure accuracy, proper formatting, and consistency with agreed commercial terms.

- Ensure proposals, budgets, and contract modifications accurately reflect customer requirements, internal strategy discussions, and approved financial assumptions.

- Collaborate with internal teams and customers throughout the budget negotiation and contract modification process to support timely agreement and contract execution.

- Identify opportunities to improve pricing, budgeting, and contract management processes to increase efficiency, accuracy, and consistency.

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent and relevant formal academic / vocational qualification.

- Experience with financial modeling, pricing analysis, contract proposals, or budgeting processes preferred.

- Strong analytical and quantitative skills with an understanding of financial budgeting and pricing principles.

- Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word, including the ability to use advanced Excel formulas for financial analysis and budget preparation.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate financial information and recommendations clearly to internal and external stakeholders.

- Effective organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities while consistently delivering accurate, high-quality work.

- Ability to work independently, prioritize responsibilities, exercise sound judgment, and take ownership of assigned projects.

- Strong attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and adaptability to changing business requirements and deadlines.

- Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and build positive working relationships.

jobs.title: Small-Cap Growth Equity Strategy Associate Analyst
jobs.description:
At T. Rowe Price, we identify and actively invest in opportunities to help people thrive in an evolving world. As a premier global asset management organization with more than 85 years of experience, we provide investment solutions and a broad range of equity, fixed income, and multi-asset capabilities to individuals, advisors, institutions, and retirement plan sponsors. We take an active, independent approach to investing, offering our dynamic perspective and meaningful partnership so our clients can feel more confident.

We believe doing the right thing for our clients and our associates is good business. With a career at the firm, you can expect opportunities to create real impact at work and in your community. You’ll enjoy resources to support your career path, as well as compensation, benefits, and flexibility to enrich your life. Here, you’ll find a collaborative culture that respects and values differences and colleagues who share a spirit of generosity.

Join us for the opportunity to grow and make a difference in ways that matter to you.

Role Summary

- The Associate Analyst will provide fundamental research support to the Portfolio Manager and team of T. Rowe Price’s Small-Cap Growth Equity Strategy, including the New Horizons Fund, one of the firm’s flagship funds and the oldest small-cap growth fund in America.

- This is a generalist role that spans all sectors across both public and private markets. The Associate Analyst will report to the Head of the Associate Analyst Program, work with the team’s Associate Analyst and Portfolio Managers, and will be responsible for: new idea generation, running analysis on the fund and fund holdings, diligence and executing private investments, and other ad-hoc assignments related to the fund.

- The fund focuses on long-term oriented, non-linear outcomes in emerging technologies (examples include AI hardware and applications, robotics, the application of AI in biotechnology/material sciences/commerce and understanding how existing companies can improve from new technologies). The candidate should have a high level of creativity and an interest in understanding the underlying technology and industries of the portfolio holdings in-depth.

- Beyond traditional fundamental research, the Associate Analyst will help design and build AI-enabled tools that streamline and scale the team’s investment process. The team views this as a core part of its edge and one that rewards creativity and thoughtful design as much as technical skill. This will be one of the main responsibilities of the role and candidates are expected to have experience building AI-enabled tools/projects and have a design thinking orientation.

- The Associate Analyst program is a three-to-five-year structured program that offers ongoing training and mentoring and is designed to develop future fundamental investment analysts.

- Competitive compensation with significant upside potential for high performers.

- Exceptional performers have the potential to be promoted to Investment Analyst.

Responsibilities

- Generate new investment ideas across the strategy’s investment universe and complete industrials analyses on emerging trends. Strong work ethic and the abilities to balance multiple projects is required.

- Build industry and market-share models to understand industry structure, addressable market size, and unit economics.

- Help design and build AI-enabled tools and workflows that streamline and scale the team’s investment process, partnering with the firm’s data and technology teams as needed. Strong candidates will be able to take the tools the strategy currently uses and be able to innovate and improve on this work.

- Own the team’s alternative data effort, including designing and running surveys, organizing channel checks/expert networks, procuring new data sources, and maintaining regular summaries and prioritizing data signals.

- Support the ongoing monitoring of portfolio holdings, including evaluating earnings and company updates against the team’s framework, maintaining focused models tailored to the fund’s fundamental thesis, and attending company meetings and sell-side/industry events.

- Collaborate regularly with the firm’s analysts, sector heads, and sector portfolio managers to stay current on positioning and emerging investment trends, and support their work and running deep analysis on these investments.

- Partner with the team on private investments, including sourcing deals, conducting due diligence and underwriting, and helping maintain portfolio company relationships.

- Participate in the fund’s team-wide responsibilities, including investment committee meetings, monthly stock pitches and position re-underwrites, and travel for conferences and company visits.

- Expectation to provide investment insight and impact the investment process beyond just number crunching.

Qualifications

Required:

- Bachelor’s degree with a strong academic record.

- 0-3 years of relevant work experience.

- Strong Excel and financial modeling skills.

- A deep and demonstrable passion for the equity investing

- Comfort with the non-linear nature of growth investing and work ethic to uncover new ideas before the market does

- A strong interest in and aptitude for using AI tools, along with a creative, design-oriented approach to building technology that improves an investment process.

Preferred:

- Prior experience in investment research, investment banking, consulting, artificial intelligence, sciences, or a related analytical field.

- Familiarity with LLMs, AI coding tools such as Claude Code or Codex, and a background in computer science or data science.

- Interest in technology and sciences, and a desire to deeply understand these companies and industries in-depth.

- Knowledge of the AI industry and the technology shaping it, with a strong interest in how those developments create investment opportunities.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- A love for learning, especially when it comes to emerging technologies/industries.

FINRA Requirements

FINRA licenses are not required and will not be supported for this role.

Work Flexibility

This role is eligible for hybrid work, with up to one day per week from home.

Applicants for employment in the US must have work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States (e.g., H1-B visa, F-1 visa (OPT), TN visa or any other non-immigrant work status).

WHAT TO EXPECT AFTER APPLYING

1. You will receive an email and text message to answer a few questions to verify your eligibility. If you apply for multiple jobs, you will receive separate invitations for each role and will need to respond to each. Estimated Time Commitment: 3-5 minutes

2. If you are eligible, you will be asked to record video responses to introductory questions with our vendor partner, HireVue. Take time to read all instructions carefully before responding. Some questions may require you to respond within a set time limit, or with limited retakes. You can use this opportunity to tell us more about your background and interest than we can learn from a resume alone. Estimated Time Commitment: 20-30 minutes

At T. Rowe Price, our associates are our greatest asset. We thrive because our company culture is built on inclusion and because we sustain a work environment where associates can bring their best selves to work every day. The backgrounds, talents, and experiences of our global associates allow us to embrace new ideas and perspectives that move our business priorities forward and enable us to deliver strong client outcomes. Here, you can expect equal opportunity and fair and consistent treatment for all.

Benefits

We value your goals and needs, at work and in life. As an associate, you’ll be supported with resources, benefits, and work-life balance so you can thrive in ways that matter to you.

Competitive compensation

Annual bonus eligibility

Hybrid work schedule

Health and wellness benefits, including online therapy

Paid time off for vacation, illness, medical appointments, and volunteering days

jobs.title: AI Research Scientist, New Grad – Agents & Reinforcement Learning
jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don't just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset, rapidly testing emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

Snowflake is about empowering enterprises to achieve their full potential, and people too. With a culture that's all in on impact, innovation, and collaboration, Snowflake is the sweet spot for building big, moving fast, and taking technology and careers to the next level.

We are hiring an AI Research Scientist (New Grad) for our AI Research team. Our team is pushing the frontier of autonomous, self-improving AI systems — building agents that reason, code, and learn at scale inside the Snowflake Data Cloud. This role sits at the intersection of agentic AI and reinforcement learning, where your research will directly shape how enterprises leverage intelligent automation.




AS AN AI RESEARCH SCIENTIST AT SNOWFLAKE, YOU WILL:

 - Design and develop agentic frameworks powered by recursive self-improvement loops, enabling AI systems that iteratively refine their own capabilities and strategies

 - Build and evaluate auto research agents — systems capable of autonomously formulating hypotheses, executing experiments, and synthesizing findings

 - Develop coding agents that understand, generate, and debug code across complex, multi-step programming tasks

 - Conduct research in reinforcement learning with a focus on RLHF, DPO, and PPO as mechanisms for aligning and improving agentic behaviors

 - Contribute to multi-agent systems where specialized agents collaborate, negotiate, and self-organize to solve enterprise-scale problems

 - Develop and curate training data pipelines — both synthetic and human-annotated — to support novel agentic and RL research domains

 - Publish research findings at top-tier venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, and ACL




OUR IDEAL AI RESEARCH SCIENTIST WILL HAVE:

 - PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, or a closely related field (completing or recently completed; or equivalent research experience)

 - Foundational expertise in reinforcement learning algorithms, including RLHF, DPO, PPO, or multi-agent systems

 - Research experience in LLM post-training, fine-tuning, or reasoning model development

 - Demonstrated ability to implement and experiment with agentic architectures — including tool-use, planning, and self-correction loops

 - Proficiency in Python and at least one deep learning framework (PyTorch or JAX strongly preferred)

 - Strong mathematical and analytical foundation — comfortable working at the intersection of theory and empirical research

 - At least one first-author or co-authored publication or preprint in a relevant AI/ML area




BONUS POINTS FOR THE FOLLOWING:

 - Hands-on experience building or evaluating coding agents or auto research agents

 - Familiarity with recursive self-improvement frameworks or automated AI scientist paradigms

 - Experience with large-scale distributed training or efficient training paradigms

 - Background in mathematical reasoning, structured decision-making, or program synthesis

 - Exposure to domain-specific AI applications in healthcare, finance, or enterprise workflows




WHY JOIN OUR AI RESEARCH TEAM AT SNOWFLAKE?

Snowflake's AI Research team operates at the frontier of what autonomous AI systems can do — not as a research lab disconnected from practice, but as a team where your work ships into a platform used by thousands of enterprises. You'll be working alongside researchers and engineers who are building the next generation of agentic infrastructure, with access to large-scale compute, real-world data challenges, and the shortest possible path from research idea to product impact.

For a new grad role, this is a rare opportunity to grow your research career while contributing to systems that actually run in production — shaping how AI agents reason, learn, and improve themselves inside the world's leading data cloud.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

jobs.title: Ad Product Quality Analyst I
jobs.description:
Snap Inc is a technology company. We believe the camera presents the greatest opportunity to improve the way people live and communicate. Snap contributes to human progress by empowering people to express themselves, live in the moment, learn about the world, and have fun together.

The Company operates Snapchat, a visual messaging app that enhances your relationships with friends, family, and the world, and Specs Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary dedicated to making computing more human, in addition to Bitmoji, Saturn, and other digital services.

We are looking for a talented and experienced business and data analyst to join the Ad Product Quality team at Snap. As an Ad Product Quality Analyst, you will be responsible for growing Snapchat’s advertising business by solving tough customer challenges and identifying opportunities to improve the quality of our monetization product offerings.

What you'll do:

- Troubleshoot Snap’s web-based advertising platform and mobile app to reproduce and root-cause client-impacting issues and expedite bug fixes

- Leverage technical skills and product expertise to triage, investigate, and resolve technical issues preventing Snap’s customers from succeeding on our ads platform as quickly and efficiently as possible

- Organize training sessions that enable our frontline support teams to assist customers encountering challenges on the platform

- Maintain a backlog of software bugs and product improvements, and serve as a customer advocate as you prioritize the most impactful open issues with Product and Engineering teams

- Partner with our Product Marketing, Sales, and Support teams to collect customer feedback and identify opportunities to improve our products

- Derive quantitative and qualitative insights into ads products usage, systems stability, and the customer experience. Produce trend analyses of common customer pain points coupled with actionable recommendations for addressing them

- Perform pre-release QA and UAT to ensure product releases and updates work as intended and do not disrupt the customer experience

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

- Ad-platform troubleshooting and quality

- Customer-impact analysis and prioritization

- Cross-functional execution and communication

Minimum qualifications

- Bachelor’s Degree in STEM or related areas of study or equivalent industry experience

- 1+ years work experience in digital advertising, operations, or a related field

Preferred qualifications:

- Experience troubleshooting front- and back-end web applications

- Experience sizing the impact of client-facing issues and setting priority

- Experience working with large data sets using SQL, Python, and other tools, and producing practical business insights via data visualization software (Looker, Tableau, etc.)

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills with high attention to detail

- Project management skills, identifying problems areas, designing solutions, and driving them to completion

- Experience with agile product development lifecycle using Jira or similar software

- Proficient in use of G Suite software (Gmail, Google Docs, Google Sheets, etc.)

"Default Together" Policy at Snap: At Snap Inc. we believe that being together in person helps us build our culture faster, reinforce our values, and serve our community, customers and partners better through dynamic collaboration. To reflect this, we practice a “default together” approach and expect our team members to work in an office 4+ days per week.

At Snap, we believe that having a team of diverse backgrounds and voices working together will enable us to create innovative products that improve the way people live and communicate. Snap is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and committed to providing employment opportunities regardless of race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding, age, sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other protected classification, in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. EOE, including disability/vets.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable law (by example, the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, where applicable).

Our Benefits: Snap Inc. is its own community, so we’ve got your back! We do our best to make sure you and your loved ones have everything you need to be happy and healthy, on your own terms. Our benefits are built around your needs and include paid parental leave, comprehensive medical coverage, emotional and mental health support programs, and compensation packages that let you share in Snap’s long-term success!

Compensation

In the United States, work locations are assigned a pay zone which determines the salary range for the position. The successful candidate’s starting pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. The starting pay may be negotiable within the salary range for the position. These pay zones may be modified in the future.

The base hourly range for this position is $35.09-$52.4 hourly.

Zone B:
The base hourly range for this position is $33.17-$50 hourly.

Zone C:
The base hourly range for this position is $29.8-$44.71 hourly.

jobs.title: Configuration Management Analyst I (Software Systems)
jobs.description:
Sierra Space Careers:

At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.

Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.

Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.

We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.

About the Role
The Software Configuration Management Analyst I is responsible for supporting programs prior to and within the Product Lifecyle Management (PLM) system to ensure all software products comply with all enterprise and program requirements. This role is focused on but not limited to Software products ranging from ground support application, test and flight software. This role involves managing software documentation and change process for software products, assigning and monitoring part numbers, and reviewing documentation for compliance and completeness. It is an entry-level position suitable for individuals with a basic understanding of configuration management concepts, software development practices and a keen eye for detail.

In this role, you will interface with software engineers, program management and system engineering to facilitate the production of artifacts that define complex software products, through initial creation, formal changes, and into final production documentation. . You will manage a catalogue of software artifacts, assign and monitor document and part numbers, and review documentation for compliance and completeness. Following detailed instructions, you will perform tasks under supervision and ensure compliance with configuration management concepts, document control, and version control practices during all phases of software change management.

About You

Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission.

We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Qualifications:

- Requires Bachelor's degree in a related field (or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree).

- Typically entry-level 0 - 2 years of experience.

- Good communication skills.

- Basic understanding of configuration management tools and software.

- Proficiency with common software configuration tools (GIT…).

- Familiarity with configuration management concepts, document control, and version control practices.

- Capable of following detailed instructions.

- Understanding of basic engineering and technical terminology.

- Ability to perform tasks under supervision.

- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience with specific configuration management tools and software.

- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.

- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

- Experience in an engineering or technical environment.

Compensation:

Pay Range:
$60,885.00 - $83,717.25

Your actual base compensation will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related knowledge and skills, education, experience, internal equity and market competitiveness.

Elevate Your Career

At Sierra Space, we are committed to your personal and professional development. We empower you to make profound and meaningful contributions and foster a vibrant culture of collaboration, where teamwork ignites breakthrough innovations.

We also offer a generous benefit package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with 150% match up to 6%, life insurance, 3 weeks paid time off, and more.

Sierra Space is an industry-leading space and defense technology company providing satellites, spacecraft, and enabling mission systems and components. We deliver mission-proven technologies to our customers that safeguard our nation, protect space-based assets and enable space exploration.

jobs.title: Program Financial Analyst I
jobs.description:
Are you looking for an opportunity to use your analysis and finance skills in a meaningful work environment that supports and protects explorers and heroes? Join our team! The Program Financial Analyst I is responsible for reviewing, monitoring, and controlling project data to support internal and external project reporting. This role involves preparing budgets and schedules for contract work, assisting with cost proposals, pricing documentation, and performing cost variance analysis to ensure realistic contract cost and schedule baselines are maintained.

The Mission Solutions and Technologies (MST) business area provides affordable, turn-key command/control, communications, integrated ISR, force protection and security solutions worldwide. The MST team has a long legacy of supporting the Department of Defense, Department of Homeland Security, commercial and international customers with years of experience in platform operations, engineering and full lifecycle management across domains – air, land, sea, space and cyber.

Responsibilities:

- Provide pricing documentation to be utilized in proposal development including ‘what-if’ program cost analysis

- Provide assistance in development of payment plans (Milestone, CLIN Liquidation, etc.)

- Assist in the utilization of product oriented or Business Area specific work breakdown structures (WBS) with responsibility assignment matrixes, WBS dictionaries, milestones, baseline establishment, and budgeting of projects/tasks

- Provide assistance in timely completion of PMPs and program baseline upon Contract Negotiation

- Review of Cobra budget data, ensuring budgets tie to program baseline and are not exceeding contract value
