jobs.title: Associate Data Scientist, DIBI
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

JOB SUMMARY

The Defense Industrial Base Institute at Northeastern University (NU) – a rapidly growing defense focused institute that conducts cutting-edge applied R&D – is seeking an experienced and highly capable Jr. Data Scientist with expertise in applying methods/frameworks/systems that apply ML&AI. The Jr. Data Scientist will operate as part of a multi-disciplinary team (academia, industry and government) and will contribute directly to the successful execution of federally funded projects/activities,

Responsibilities include providing technical expertise and analytical support to Principal investigators or co-principal investigators as a Jr. Data Scientist for a wide range of projects and activities involving machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI), including autonomy, sensing and communication, and decision support systems, among others. The Jr, Data Scientist will work collaboratively with and help guide, multi-disciplinary teams across the DIBI Higher Education Consortium — spanning academic, government, and industry partners — to design, validate, and maintain datasets and analytical products that inform institute leadership and sponsor decision-making. Specifically, the Jr. Data Scientist will take a role in building and maintaining the data pipelines and analytical components underlying the existing Navigator methodology, working closely with — and providing guidance to — data researchers, engineers, and leadership across the institute.

Successful candidates will be responsible team players and passionate about machine learning technologies, as well as possess a deep understanding of machine learning technology and experience in turning machine learning systems into practical, state-of-the-art systems that can be enhanced for projects or activities as per federal agency. A close working relationship with the team, along with creative thinking on the application of the Navigator framework for government and industry contracts, will be required.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

The Transportation Analyst I provides day-to-day operational and analytical support for Milwaukee Tool’s transportation network. Serving as a first point of contact for transportation-related needs. This role coordinates inbound and outbound shipments, supports carrier performance and compliance, resolves service issues, manages freight claims, carrier invoice payment exceptions, and identifies opportunities to improve quality, service, and costs. The analyst partners across the organization to deliver reliable transportation solutions and uses data to support fact-based decisions and continuous improvement. Success in this role requires strong communication, problem-solving, and analytical skills, along with proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Power BI, AI tools, and PowerPoint.

You’ll be DISRUPTIVE through these duties and responsibilities:

- Coordinate inbound and outbound transportation activities, including shipment scheduling, routing, booking, tracking, expediting, and delivery follow-up.

- Partner cross-functionally with Supply Planning, Sourcing, Service, Manufacturing, Sales, Merchandising, Distribution, suppliers, and carriers to support business and customer requirements.

- Monitor daily shipment activity and proactively resolve lost, misrouted, delayed, or damaged freight with carriers and internal stakeholders.

- Provide freight quotes and secure carrier capacity for expedited, ad hoc, and special shipment requests.

- Evaluate expedited shipment requests and recommend the most cost-effective service option; escalate excess-cost transactions for appropriate approval.

- Develop and maintain routing guides, supplier requirements, and transportation compliance standards that balance service, quality, and cost objectives.

- Analyze freight and routing data to identify noncompliance, service gaps, cost drivers, and process-improvement opportunities.

- Track carrier performance across transportation modes, communicate results, and escalate recurring service issues for corrective action.

- Manage freight claims, including claim submission, documentation, follow-up, and recovery tracking.

- Research and resolve transportation-related customer issues in collaboration with carriers and the broader distribution network.

- Support freight payment exception resolution and help ensure transportation charges are accurate and appropriately documented.

- Lead or support data-driven cost mitigation and continuous-improvement initiatives.

- Provide operational coverage and support for the Transportation Manager as needed.

The TOOLS you’ll bring with you:

- 0-2 years of experience in transportation, logistics, supply chain, or a related operational environment preferred.· Bachelor’s degree in transportation, operations, logistics, supply chain management, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant education and experience will be considered.

- Ability to extract, organize, manipulate, and interpret transportation and operational data.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate findings into practical recommendations.

- Effective written and verbal communication skills for working with carriers, suppliers, customers, and internal business partners.

- Ability to manage multiple priorities, respond to time-sensitive issues, and maintain attention to detail in a fast-paced environment.

- Demonstrated ability to collaborate across functions and contribute within a one-team environment.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Power BI, and PowerPoint.

- Generous 401 (K) savings plan

- Education assistance

- On-site wellness, fitness center, food, and coffee service

We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.

Job Summary
Across the healthcare industry nationwide, hospitals and health systems face challenges to today’s approaches to expense management, as revenue growth has not kept pace with expense growth. In response to these unprecedented external challenges, MGB launched Sustain in fall of 2023. Sustain is an ongoing organization-wide program that works to build an infrastructure, culture, and mindset around continuous improvement, working to preserve our four-part mission through focus on resource stewardship. To do this, while also funding needed capital maintenance and improvements to deliver on world-class patient care, research, education, and community health, we must seek out innovative opportunities to optimize the way we work and manage resources across our organization.

The Sustain Analytics team is part of the Business Planning department, which also includes Decision Support and Business Analytics teams. The Business Analyst (Finance), on the Sustain Analytics team is responsible for supporting a broad range of analytic, planning, benchmarking, and other operational support activities for one or more designated members of the Leadership Team (Senior VP’s, Clinical VP’s, Operating VP’s and Executive Directors), across the enterprise, under the guidance of senior team members.

A critical measure of each Business Analyst’s success will be the extent to which the analytic and planning needs of each person supported are met in a timely, consistent, high quality manner. This will require close collaboration with staff within the clinical departments, and many other analytic, financial, and planning groups throughout the MGB enterprise, including Sustain Management Office (SMO), Business Planning, Financial Planning, Digital, and local financial, operational, and analytical teams and decision-making bodies at each of the MGB entities. An ability to synthesize, summarize and effectively communicate the analytic and planning work that is performed is key.

- Experience working in a health system, hospital and/or similar medical center environment preferred.

jobs.title: Software Management Analyst I
jobs.description:
Are you interested in helping employees get the software they need while supporting accurate, cost-effective license management?

Would you like to build your software asset management skills in a role where organization, customer service, and attention to detail make a real impact?

About our Team

LexisNexis Legal & Professional, which serves customers in more than 150 countries with 11,800 employees worldwide, is part of RELX (http://www.relx.com), a global provider of information-based analytics and decision tools for professional and business customers. Our company has been a long-time leader in deploying AI and advanced technologies to the legal market to improve productivity and transform the overall business and practice of law, deploying ethical and powerful generative AI solutions with a flexible, multi-model approach that prioritizes using the best model from today’s top model creators for each individual legal use case. The company employs over 2,000 technologists, data scientists, and experts to develop, test, and validate solutions in line with RELX Responsible AI Principles (https://stories.relx.com/responsible-ai-principles/index.html).

About the Role

You will support day-to-day software asset management activities, helping employees receive approved software and ensuring license and inventory records stay current. You will process requests, provision and reclaim licenses, provide customer support, and contribute to routine reporting and process improvements.

Responsibilities

- Fulfill software requests: Review and process ServiceNow tickets, confirm required approvals, and complete requests within established service levels.

- Provision software: Assign approved licenses, provide access or installation instructions, and coordinate with IT support when needed.

- Reclaim unused licenses: Review usage reports, contact users to confirm ongoing needs, and remove or reassign licenses according to established procedures.

- Maintain accurate records: Update license assignments, subscription details, software inventory, and ticket documentation.

jobs.title: Flow Cytometry Analyst I
jobs.description:
Labcorp is a global leader in laboratory services, providing the insights and answers that help healthcare providers, patients, researchers, pharmaceutical companies and health systems make confident decisions and improve outcomes. Through our unparalleled science, data, technology and laboratory network, we advance diagnostics, accelerate innovation and help address some of the world’s most important health challenges. As we shape the future of healthcare, we are leveraging advanced technologies, intelligent digital solutions and data-driven innovation across our operations to enhance how work gets done and deliver greater value to customers and patients. With our global scale and deep expertise, you’ll have the opportunity to do meaningful work, grow your career and make a real impact on people’s health around the world. Together, we’re improving health and improving lives.

Labcorp is seeking a Flow Cytometry Analyst I to join our Flow Cytometry team in Indianapolis, IN!

Work Schedule: Monday-Friday 8am-4:30pm or 9am-5:30pm

The Flow Cytometry Analyst I plays a key role in supporting accurate and timely patient sample analysis across a wide range of flow cytometry assays. This position is responsible for analyzing flow cytometry data using established analysis software, including WinList and FCS Express, and accurately preparing and saving results using assay-specific Excel tools. Analysts follow established analysis procedures and assay-specific training materials to ensure consistent, accurate, and high-quality results.

The role may also support the analysis of technical transfer samples as new assays are transitioned into the laboratory. The ideal candidate will have a solid foundation in flow cytometry, strong analytical skills, excellent attention to detail, and proficiency in using Microsoft Excel, including accurately entering, reviewing, saving, and managing analysis files. The ability to learn and work with multiple assays and software platforms, manage competing priorities, and consistently follow established procedures is essential for success in this role.

Key Responsibilities:

· Perform Flow Cytometry Data Analysis: Analyze patient sample data across a wide range of assays using established analysis software, including WinList and FCS Express, following approved assay-specific analysis procedures, templates, and training materials to ensure accurate and consistent results.

· Utilize Established Analysis Tools: Learn and effectively use existing analysis software, gating templates, Excel reporting tools, and assay-specific training materials to perform analysis according to established procedures.

· Ensure Analysis Accuracy and Quality: Review analyzed patient sample data for accuracy and consistency, applying established assay-specific analysis criteria and escalating unusual findings or issues when appropriate.

· Prepare and Save Analysis Results: Generate and maintain patient sample result files using established reporting workflows. Depending on the assay and analysis platform, this may include saving system-generated results or preparing result Excel files from analysis-generated capture data. Ensure final results are accurately saved and maintained in the required Excel and PDF formats according to established procedures.

· Support Technical Transfers: Analyze technical transfer data using established analysis procedures and prepare the associated Excel and PDF result files. Perform accurate and consistent analysis of technical transfer samples and prepare the associated Excel and PDF result files to support evaluation against established acceptance criteria, including applicable CV% requirements.

· Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Work with Scientists and other team members as needed to address analysis questions, unusual data patterns, or assay-specific considerations while following established gating and analysis strategies.

· Maintain Documentation & Compliance: Uphold rigorous documentation, data integrity, and quality standards in alignment with departmental procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.

Minimum Qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree in a Chemical or Biological science, Clinical Laboratory Science, or Medical Technology.

- 1 year of flow cytometry analysis experience including FCS Express

Preferred Qualifications:

- Two years of experience with flow cytometry analysis

- MT(ASCP), MLS(ASCP), CLS(NCA) or SCYM(ASCP) certification

Additional Job Standards:

- Ability to work independently and within a remote global team environment

- Proficient with computers; Familiarity with laboratory information systems

- High level of attention to detail along with strong communication and organizational skills

- Able to pass a standardized color blindness test

- Flexibility to work overtime or other shifts depending on business needs

- Strong working knowledge of flow cytometry principles

- Hands-on experience with FCS Express or comparable analysis software; experience with Excel automation (macros, formulas) preferred.

- Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality results under tight timelines.

- Detail-oriented with excellent problem-solving, documentation, and communication skills.

Pay Range: All job offers will be based on a candidate’s skills and prior relevant experience, applicable degrees/certifications, as well as internal equity and market data.

At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. The position is an entry-level role that supports the Company’s global lease accounting and financial reporting processes. Working under direct supervision and established procedures. The analyst will review lease agreement, prepare lease analysis, maintain accurate lease data, and support lease disclosures for the Company’s external financial reports.

The role requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work collaboratively with various cross-functional partners to obtain complete and accurate information. · Research lease accounting guidance and document conclusions for routine accounting questions, with guidance from senior team members.

· Complete ad hoc analyses and special projects as requested by management.

• Bachelor’s degree in Accounting.

• 0-2 years of experience.

• The ability to identify, understand a problem and its root cause, and research effective solutions.

jobs.title: Startup Generalist (New Grad)
jobs.description:
ABOUT HYPHENATE 

Most AI companies are building copilots.

Hyphenate is building the AI operating system for the CFO office. Our Audit-Ready AI Agents connect to a company's existing finance stack—ERPs, banks, billing, payroll, CRM, contracts, spreadsheets, email, and Slack—and automate the work behind the entire order-to-cash process, record-to-report process, treasury management, financial reporting, and audit readiness.

The goal isn't to help the finance team write better prompts.

The goal is for finance teams to review exceptions while AI does the rest.

What makes Hyphenate different is our Unified Finance Context—a financial understanding layer that captures transactions, policies, contracts, historical decisions, and accounting judgment. On top of it sit Audit-Ready AI Agents that can reason, explain their decisions, escalate uncertainty, and continuously improve.

We've raised $9M led by Foundation Capital, alongside BoldCap, Gaia Ventures, Aravind Srinivas (CEO of Perplexity), and finance leaders from Zuora, Ramp, Gusto, MongoDB, Zoom, and the Big Four.




THE ROLE

We can't tell you what you'll be doing six months from now. That's not vagueness—that's the job.

You'll work directly with the founders on whatever matters most that week. Some weeks that means sitting with a controller at 9pm during close, watching which spreadsheet she opens first and why. Some weeks it's the ROI model that unblocks an enterprise deal. Some weeks it's the research piece that names a problem the whole industry has been quietly working around.

We're defining a category that doesn't exist yet. Categories don't get defined by the product alone—they get defined by the arguments you make, the benchmarks you publish, the rooms you get people into, and the language the market ends up borrowing from you.

That work needs an owner. It doesn't need a specialist.




WHAT THE WORK ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE

Learn how finance teams really work. Sit in on sales calls, implementations, and support threads. Visit customers. Watch a close happen end to end. Read every piece of feedback we get. Nobody at Hyphenate is more valuable than the person who understands the customer best—and that spot is open.

Sharpen how we decide. Size a market. Pull apart a competitor's pricing. Interview ten controllers and turn it into a point of view we didn't have. Build the board deck. Write the memo that settles an argument.

Build things. Not just recommend them. Prototype the internal tool with Claude. Run the pricing analysis. Ship the customer event. Launch the research report. Stand up the metrics dashboard nobody else has time for.

Help define the category. Original research, customer stories, founder content, conference talks, and relationships across the accounting and finance world. We want to be a company people learn from, not just buy from.




PROBLEMS WORTH YOUR BRAIN

 - How do you price software that replaces work instead of tooling? Seat-based pricing breaks when the product does the job instead of helping someone do it.

 - How do you prove ROI for an agent? Finance teams buy on evidence. What's the honest, defensible number, and how do you get it?

 - What actually makes a controller trust software? Not a demo. Something else. Go find out what.

 - How do you turn fifty scattered customer conversations into one decision? Synthesis is a skill. Most people are bad at it.

 - How do you build a category from nothing? Nobody is searching for "Audit-Ready AI for Finance" yet. Change that.




A FEW STRONG OPINIONS

 - The generalist who can build beats three who can only recommend. Fluency with Claude and other AI tools isn't a bonus here—it's how one person does the work of a team. You should be automating your own job by month three.

 - Writing is thinking. We'd rather read a sharp two-page memo than sit through a twenty-slide deck. If you can't write it clearly, you don't understand it yet.

 - The accountant + engineer loop is the moat. The people who sit with controllers and build from what they see compound faster than the ones who don't. That includes you.

 - We hire for slope, not intercept. How fast you learn matters more than what you already know. We'd rather teach you finance than teach you how to think.

 - Titles here are temporary. Where this role goes in two years depends almost entirely on what you turn out to be good at. Several of the best jobs at this company don't exist yet.




WHO YOU ARE

We care much more about how you think than what's on your résumé.

 - Zero to two years of experience, or finishing your degree now. Any field.

 - You've done something analytical and hard. Consulting, banking, product, engineering, research, journalism, a startup—or you've built and run something on your own. Both count equally.

 - You write clearly. This is the filter that matters most. Clear writing is the visible output of clear thinking.

 - You use AI to do real work. Not as a novelty. You've built something with Claude, or automated a process, or gotten an agent to do something genuinely useful.

 - You're unusually curious. You're the person who goes three levels deeper than the question required, because you couldn't help it.

 - You want responsibility earlier than is comfortable. You'll get it.

You don't need a finance background. You don't need an AI background. You need to be someone who gets obsessed with things.




YOU'LL STAND OUT IF

 - You've shipped something real without an engineer—a tool, an automation, a product, a business.

 - You've written something publicly that people actually read.

 - You've worked at a startup under thirty people and liked the chaos.

 - You have an accounting or finance background—Big Four, audit, FP&A, controllership. That's rarer than you'd think and unusually valuable here.

 - You studied something quantitative and you can write. That combination is the whole job.

 - You've run something end to end where nobody was checking your work.

 - You're curious about how money actually moves.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AFTER A YEAR

 - You're one of the first people the founders pull into a hard decision.

 - Customers ask for you by name, because you've spent real time learning from them.

 - You've launched at least two things that didn't exist when you joined.

 - You've written something you'd put your name on publicly—and we published it.

 - You've had more ownership than most people get in five years somewhere larger.




THIS PROBABLY ISN'T FOR YOU IF

 - You want a defined scope and a clear ladder. Neither exists here yet.

 - You'd rather analyze the decision than own the outcome.

 - You want to work remotely. This role in particular is learned by proximity.

 - You need the work to be interesting on day one. Some of it is unglamorous, and the unglamorous parts are often where the leverage is.




THE UPSIDE

 - Direct, daily access to founders, customers, CFOs, controllers, and investors.

 - Competitive pay and meaningful early-stage equity.

 - Full medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, plus 401(k) match.

 - Meals, a stocked NYC office, and the chance to help define an entirely new category: Audit-Ready AI for Finance.
   
   


THE DETAILS

 - In-person in New York City. Five days a week, in the same room as the founders. That's the point of the job.

 - This is an early-career role by design. We're hiring for trajectory, not for a résumé.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. Partners with the businesses to ensure that the capital strategies are operationally supported and strategically focused to secure the greatest return on investment for the global company. Gathers financial data and performs financial analyses and reporting (e.g., profit & loss, balance sheet, cash flow, pricing, etc.) to influence decisions within the business and to drive cross-business initiatives (e.g., Mergers & Acquisitions). Drives the forecasting process (weekly, monthly, and long term) by analyzing trends within the businesses and ensuring alignment with business- and corporate-wide objectives. Communicates and drives adherence to Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and the organization's financial goals and policies. - Performs data extraction and analyzes data to make recommendations.

- Handles financial business issues.

- Provides analytics to business initiatives

- Develops an understanding of the company's financial processes and a working knowledge of the business.

Education and Experience Required:

- Basic analytical skills.

- Good business application skills (e.g., Microsoft Excel).

- Good teamwork skills.

jobs.title: Financial Analyst I
jobs.description:
Company Description
By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.

Financial Administration (FAD) is dedicated to advancing Harvard University’s teaching and research mission by stewarding its resources; providing support, guidance, and consultation; ensuring compliance with university and federal guidelines; mitigating risk; pursuing operational excellence; and promoting the financial health of the University.

More about FAD:

Within and across the University, we aim to be exemplary colleagues, trusted partners, valued advisors, and agents of positive change.

Within our own community, we aspire to:

- Engage with respect, honesty, and integrity

- Cultivate equity, diversity, inclusion, and belonging

- Welcome innovation, collaboration, and flexibility

- Enjoy our work, grow professionally, and aim for the extraordinary

Learn more about Financial Administration (harvard.edu) and our eight reporting units. (https://finance.harvard.edu/)

Job Description
The Office for Sponsored Programs is a department within Harvard University’s Financial Administration (FAD) that is focused on providing high-quality administrative and financial assistance to faculty and other University affiliates performing sponsored research. OSP works with researchers and schools across Harvard to help obtain and negotiate awards from sponsoring agencies, assist with grant proposal preparation, ensure compliance with federal regulations and University policies, provide financial support including financial reporting and billing and collection services, assist with audits, and promote knowledge of sponsored research administration throughout the University research community through training and other educational programs.

The Financial Analyst I (FA I) supports the Research Finance Operations (RFO) Team in the Office for Sponsored Programs (OSP). The three core functions of this role are:

- Apply standard practices with the interpretation and recording of financial terms in the Grants Management Application Suite (GMAS)

- Prepare and submit a high volume of standardized invoices and reports to sponsors

- Monitor and facilitate the collection of outstanding accounts receivable. This role requires the ability to balance accuracy with working in a high-volume, deadline-driven environment.

The FA I is responsible for reviewing sponsored agreements for any terms related to payment and financial reporting and for setting up the schedule of invoices, financial reports (financial deliverables), and other related data in GMAS.

The FA I is also responsible for completing standard invoices and standard financial reports as assigned each month using an automated process in GMAS. In doing so, the FA I may be required to work directly with sponsors, clients, and colleagues to ensure the sponsor requirements are met.

The FA I also performs the accounts receivable collection of any outstanding sponsored payments and coordinates collections efforts with sponsors and clients when necessary.

Approximately 35% effort is anticipated for scheduling, 35% for invoicing and financial reporting, 20% for accounts receivable collection, and 10% for project-based duties, which can include business process documentation, training initiatives, account reconciliation and closeout, ad hoc data analysis, and other special projects.

Job-Specific Responsibilities:

- Serves as a principal source of information for interpreting complex financial terms and conditions within sponsored agreements

- Accurately records financial deliverable schedules and related information in the sponsored system of record (GMAS)

- Produces timely and accurate invoices and financial reports based on sponsor deadlines

- Analyzes financial data to identify potential risks and issues (quantitatively and qualitatively) in a way that is meaningful and proposes solutions for complex issues and best practices, which may require the entry of adjustments in the General Ledger

- Works within the team and across Research Finance to update and develop business processes and identify best practices

- Liaise effectively with other groups, such as sponsors, school financial offices, academic department leadership, pre-award offices, and central finance and technology units to clarify sponsor requirements, business processes, and systems

- Provides backfill support for peers or additional support during busy periods, when required, consistently applying processes and practices to new assignments

- Assists with developing and delivering metrics/reports, business process documentation, training initiatives, and special projects as needed

Qualifications
Basic Qualifications:

Basic Qualifications are the minimum threshold a candidate must meet in order to be considered for this role.

For consideration, please include a cover letter.

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience required

- 3+ years of direct accounting, financial management, data analysis, and/or grants management experience. Progress toward relevant professional certification may count toward experience.

Additional Qualifications and Skills:

The following qualifications are strongly preferred. If you meet some, but not all, you are still encouraged to apply; we value employees with a willingness to learn.

- Ability to prioritize and handle large volumes of work in a deadline driven environment

- Ability to work independently and as part of a team

- Strong attention to detail with excellent organizational and time management skills

- Ability to handle complex and confidential information with discretion and judgment

- Working knowledge of accounting and direct experience in financial management

- Experience with fund accounting or sponsored accounting

- Experience in sponsored programs or a research environment

- Problem-solving orientation and ability to be thorough and detail-oriented, but also able to summarize and convey the bigger picture

- Proven ability to utilize multiple financial and reporting systems, as well as other applications (i.e. Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Adobe)

- Demonstrated strength in written and verbal communication

Additional Information
Why join Harvard University Central Administration?

Harvard University's Central Administration (CADM) is a 5,000+ employee organization that supports the university's overall excellence by understanding and serving the needs of its schools, students, faculty, staff, alumni, and surrounding communities. Through dynamic and collaborative partnerships, CADM provides high-quality and efficient services to the schools to help them achieve their goals.

Working Conditions: Primarily remote role with flexibility to work on-site and optional in-person meetings bi-monthly. On-site attendance expectations may evolve based on business needs.

Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week

Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position

Pre-Employment Screening: Identity, Education

Other Information: This position has a 90-day orientation and review period.

Work Format Details

This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that some of the duties and responsibilities can be effectively performed at a non-Harvard location. The work schedule and location will be set by the department at its discretion and based upon operational needs. When not working at a Harvard or Harvard-designated location, employees in hybrid positions must work in a Harvard registered state in compliance with the University’s Policy on Employment Outside of Massachusetts. Additional details will be discussed during the interview process. Certain visa types and funding sources may limit work location. Individuals must meet work location sponsorship requirements prior to employment.

Salary Grade and Ranges

This position is salary grade level 055. Please visit  Harvard's Salary Ranges  to view the corresponding salary range and related information.

Benefits

Harvard offers a comprehensive benefits package that is designed to support a healthy work-life balance and your physical, mental and financial wellbeing. Because here, you are what matters. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

- Generous paid time off including parental leave

- Medical, dental, and vision health insurance coverage starting on day one

- Retirement plans with university contributions

- Wellbeing and mental health resources

- Support for families and caregivers

- Professional development opportunities including tuition assistance and reimbursement

- Commuter benefits, discounts and campus perks

Learn more about these and additional benefits on our Benefits & Wellbeing Page.

EEO/Non-Discrimination Commitment Statement

Harvard University is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination. We seek talent from all parts of society and the world, and we strive to ensure everyone at Harvard thrives. Our differences help our community advance Harvard's academic purposes.

Harvard has an equal employment opportunity policy that outlines our commitment to prohibiting discrimination on the basis of race, ethnicity, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, religion, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law or identified in the university's non-discrimination policy. Harvard's equal employment opportunity policy and non-discrimination policy help all community members participate fully in work and campus life free from harassment and discrimination.

jobs.description:
What We're Looking For
At HNTB, you can create a career that is meaningful to you while building communities that matter to all of us. For more than a century, we have been delivering solutions for some of the largest, most complex infrastructure projects across the country. With our historic growth, it is an exciting time to join our team of employee-owners. HNTB is seeking a highly motivated and talented professional to join our growing Transportation Planning Practice within the New York Planning & Environment Group. This role offers the opportunity to contribute to key transportation engineering & planning projects, including bike, ped, rail, bus and freight mobility improvements, while supporting New York City clients on a wide range of engineering & planning efforts. The successful candidate will apply advanced data analysis skills, sound traffic engineering & planning judgment, and a broad base of technical knowledge to deliver impactful solutions.

This opportunity entails being responsible for applying traffic engineering & planning strategies utilizing various technologies and tools to gather and analyze traffic data, assess outcomes, and develop reporting and visuals to effectively communicate findings. This position assists with tasks for traffic engineering & planning projects including research, studies, and documentation, coordinating with inter-disciplinary team members, from concept development through project completion.

- Performs tasks related to the preparation and production of plans, studies, reports, and environmental documents for transportation and infrastructure projects.

- Assists in stakeholder and public participation process.

- Understands GIS software and Microsoft Office Suite.

- Knowledge of USAF Acquisition Program & Technology Protection

· Establishes national and best practice benchmarks and measures performance against benchmarks.

· Ensures accurate payment by independently utilizing DRG grouper, encoder, and claims processing platform.

· Consistently demonstrates high standards of integrity by supporting the Lifetime Healthcare Companies’ mission and values, adhering to the Corporate Code of Conduct, and leading to the Lifetime Way values and beliefs.

· Regular and reliable attendance is expected and required.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Analytics Engineer II
jobs.description:
At DICK’S Sporting Goods, we believe in how positively sports can change lives. On our team, everyone plays a critical role in creating confidence and excitement by personally equipping all athletes to achieve their dreams. We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workforce, reflecting the communities we serve.

If you are ready to make a difference as part of the world’s greatest sports team, apply to join our team today!

OVERVIEW:

The Analytics Engineer II bridges business operations, Data Engineering, and Business Intelligence by applying knowledge of Supply Chain processes, system workflows, and data relationships to develop trusted data products, scalable semantic models, and AI-enabled analytical capabilities. The role is responsible for the transformation, modeling, quality, documentation, delivery of governed business-ready data assets that provide a trusted foundation for reporting, self-service analytics, operational decision-making, and AI-enabled solutions. The role partners with Data Engineering on data ingestion and platform capabilities and supports downstream analytics teams through reliable data products, governed definitions, and technical knowledge transfer.

Data Products & Analytics Solutions:

- Partner with business stakeholders, Product, and Data Engineering teams to understand Supply Chain operations, business processes, system workflows, and data requirements. Translate business needs into scalable analytics solutions that support operational decision-making and align with business objectives.

- Design, build, maintain, and enhance curated datasets, semantic models, and reusable analytical products that provide a trusted foundation for reporting, self-service analytics, operational decision-making, and AI-enabled solutions.

- Apply SQL, data transformation techniques, business logic, and data modeling practices to integrate, validate, and transform complex data into trusted, governed, and business-ready information assets that accurately reflect business processes and system workflows.

- Develop and maintain semantic layers, certified datasets, governed metrics, and business definitions that promote reporting consistency, improve data accessibility, and reduce duplication across analytics solutions.

- Prepare and optimize analytical data products, semantic models, governed business definitions, and data experiences that support AI-enabled and conversational analytics, predictive insights, and other emerging data-driven capabilities. Contribute to AI-enabled analytics use cases through semantic preparation, prompt development, and output validation, in partnership with appropriate technical and governance teams.

Data Quality, Governance & Reliability:

- Apply established standards for data quality, performance, and governance across analytical data products. Leverage business process, system, and technical knowledge to execute test plans, validate source-to-target data flows, assess data quality, and validate analytical solutions. Document, communicate, and resolve identified issues using standardized testing methodologies.

- Maintain business and technical metadata, source-to-target mappings, data lineage, ownership information, technical specifications, and supporting documentation within approved data catalog and knowledge management tools to improve discoverability, auditability, governance, and change-impact analysis.Apply enterprise data-classification, privacy, security, access-control, and retention requirements to analytical datasets, semantic models, and self-service analytics solutions. Partner with appropriate security, privacy, and governance teams to ensure compliance with established standards.

- Monitor assigned data products in production, triage data quality and reliability incidents, support recovery and escalation activities, communicate identified business impact, document root causes, implement corrective actions and contribute to preventive reliability improvements.

- Assess upstream and downstream impacts of data, schema, metric, system, and process changes. Coordinate testing, stakeholder communication, and implementation activities to ensure analytical assets remain accurate, reliable, and aligned with evolving business and system requirements.

Business & Technical Partnership:

- Develop effective working relationships with business partners to understand business processes, system workflows, data needs, and analytical challenges.

- Collaborate with Operations, Finance, Product, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, and Business Intelligence teams to support the design, delivery, and maintenance of data assets.

- Partner with internal and external teams to identify and capture new data requirements, perform root-cause analysis, and support the diagnosis and resolution of data-related issues.

Data Integration & Lifecycle Support:

- Monitor and support vendor, product, and operational data integrations (e.g. FTP, Kafka, DataStage) to ensure reliable data delivery, data quality, and availability of analytical data products.

- Collaborate with Product, Data Engineering, and technology teams on development, testing, incident resolution, and monitoring activities related to data integrations and processing workflows.

- Participate in the implementation of new data sources and data elements by supporting requirements gathering, solution design, testing, deployment, and change management activities.

Team Practices & Continuous Improvement :

- Provide technical guidance and knowledge transfer to downstream analytics teams regarding data models, semantic layers, governed metrics, data availability, and structural changes.

- Build knowledge of Supply Chain operations, business processes, system workflows, and data structures to effectively support analytical solutions and operational decision-making.

- Share knowledge and provide guidance to less experienced teammates in data analysis, troubleshooting, and analytics development activities. Support assigned planning, delivery, and continuous improvement activities.

- Maintain awareness of evolving analytics, AI-enabled analytics, business intelligence, and data management practices, applying new skills and knowledge to improve analytical solutions and team capabilities.

QUALIFICATIONS:

- Bachelor's degree - BS in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Engineering, Statistics, Supply Chain, or a related field

- Analytics engineering, business intelligence, data management, data engineering, or a related discipline.

- Experience should include proficient SQL, multi-source data transformation, dimensional or semantic modeling, data-quality testing, documentation, production support, and delivery of analytical data products.

- Demonstrated ability to understand business processes and system workflows and connect them to how data is generated, transformed, and consumed is required.

- Supply-chain or Manhattan-system experience is preferred.

- Relevant training or certifications in SQL, analytics engineering, cloud data platforms, data governance, BI tooling, or AI-enabled analytics are preferred.

- Proficiency in SQL, data transformation techniques, and data modeling concepts used to integrate, validate, and prepare data for analytical solutions

- Experience working with cloud-based data and analytics platforms (e.g. Databricks, Snowflake, Azure, AWS, Google Cloud) to support data analysis and reporting needs.

- Experience supporting data ingestion, integration, and orchestration processes using technologies such as Kafka, FTP, ETL/ELT frameworks, or similar tools.Experience developing datasets and analytical solutions using business intelligence and self-service analytics platforms (e.g. Cognos, Power BI, Qlik)

- Familiarity with metadata management, data lineage, documentation, and data catalog practices that promote data quality, discoverability, and governance.

- Experience using version control tools (e.g., Git) and applying testing, deployment, and change management, and work management practices (e.g. Jira) within the analytics development lifecycle.

- Familiarity with AI-enabled analytics, conversational analytics, predictive analytics, and related technologies used to support data-driven decision-making.

VIRTUAL REQUIREMENTS:

At DICK’S, we thrive on innovation and authenticity. That said, to protect the integrity and security of our hiring process, we ask that candidates do not use AI tools (like ChatGPT or others) during interviews or assessments.

To ensure a smooth and secure experience, please note the following:

jobs.title: Associate Consultant
jobs.description:
Our Professional Services team is expanding! We are looking to hire an Associate Consultant; this role at Deposco offers a unique opportunity to combine technical aptitude, business skills, supply chain knowledge, and face-to-face client interaction in an exciting, software consulting career. The position allows you to partner directly with industry leading customers to help them achieve supply chain and business success.
Our Associate Consultants have the opportunity to work in a variety of industries including consumer goods, food & beverage, third-party logistics, transportation and shipping, and more!
Deposco’s Solutions Consultants are the customer’s primary point of contact through the implementation of Deposco’s Bright Suite of solutions:


Bright Warehouse: Warehouse and Distribution Management

Bright Order: Distributed Order Management

Bright Source: Sourcing and Procurement

Bright Store: Inventory Management and Point of Purchase

Bright Socket: Software Integrations

Bright Performance: Business Reports and Dashboards

Bright Forecast: Demand Planning and Forecasting

Bright Inventory: Inventory Planning 



What You'll Do

Primary activities will include: 

 - Configuring, testing, issue resolution and implementation support.

 - Collaborate with clients to solve challenging business requirements

 - Analyze and resolve issues that arise throughout the implementation. 

 - Work with analysts to resolve technical issues.

 - Perform testing of client specific enhancements in a timely manner.

 - 50-65% travel required. A portion of your time will be spent on-site working directly with the customer’s project team.



What You'll Need

 - Bachelor of Science degree in Industrial Engineering; Supply Chain Management; Management Information Systems; Computer Science; or related technical degree, with a minimum overall grade point average (GPA) of 3.0

 - 0 – 1 years of experience developing, supporting or implementing application software and/or experience through internships and/or cooperative programs

 - “Hands on” work experience gained through internships and/or co-op programs, especially if supply chain related

 - Must possess an understanding of supply-chain management

 - Experience troubleshooting and developing SQL queries using relational databases

 - Excellent communications and task management skills

 - Enthusiastic and positive attitude

 - Ability to work and collaborate with team members both technically and functionally in nature

 - Self-motivated and hungry to learn

 - Ability to handle multiple projects and tasks simultaneously

 - Position located at the Alpharetta, GA office
   
   

PERKS

 - Be part of an energetic team that is serious about delivering software to customers and cultivating our culture. We work awfully hard and are having a blast doing it. This team believes that what we are doing is a game-changer in the industry

 - Coffee bar with cold brew on tap and a full time barista

 - Standing desk (if you’re into that sort of thing)

 - Corporate events including food trucks, Top Golf and other shenanigans

 - Corporate office with co-working spaces, ping-pong tables, corn-hole boards, and Avalon around the corner

 - Benefits package including health care, paid time off, life insurance, 401k plan (with match), and gym reimbursement

 - Be part of a team recognized 5 years running as an AJC Top Workplace



About Us

Deposco is a leading provider of cloud-based SaaS solutions for omni-channel fulfillment, e-commerce and supply chain operations. Deposco’s Bright Suite helps distributors, retailers, e-tailers, manufacturers, agencies and logistics providers streamline their supply chain and fulfillment operations. Our fast implementations improve profitability by increasing revenue while reducing costs, complexity, and order-to-cash cycle-time. Headquartered in Alpharetta, Georgia, Deposco (http://www.deposco.com) is a certified UPS Ready, FedEx, USPS and Canada Post integrated vendor. Recent industry awards & accolades include Gartner 2015 Cool Vendor, Internet Logistics Top 100, and Supply Chain & Demand Executive 100.

jobs.description:

At Aldevron, one of Danaher’s 15+ operating companies, our work saves lives—and we’re all united by a shared commitment to innovate for tangible impact.

You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter. And by harnessing Danaher’s system of continuous improvement, you help turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.

At Aldevron, we deliver world-class CDMO services that accelerate the development of groundbreaking therapies. Our mission is to be the engine of innovation for genomic medicine pioneers. -
Independently perform established QC assays and non-routine testing as assigned.

-
Accurately document results and perform data entry and self-review.

-
Assist with equipment maintenance and calibration.

Bachelor of Science in Biology, Biochemistry, or related field required

Independently perform established QC assays and non-routine testing as assigned

Operating precision measuring tools and laboratory equipment

DXC's Insurance Software and BPS (ISB) helps insurers around the world modernize and run their core operations at scale by combining deep industry expertise, proven software platforms, and innovative AI-driven solutions. A global market leader in core insurance platforms, ISB delivers solutions across policy administration, claims, billing, analytics, and digital engagement supporting Life & Annuity, Property & Casualty, and Specialty insurance markets. You’ll directly shape how the world's leading insurers operate by helping to transform the policy, underwriting, and claims systems that millions of people rely on every day.

About the Role

The Plan Services & Operations Specialist plays a key role in supporting complex retirement and annuity operations, including plan audits and reporting, financial reconciliation, complex service resolution, complaint research, and fraud-related matters. This role is essential to maintaining the integrity and accuracy of plan servicing activities, ensuring that operational issues are identified, researched, and resolved in accordance with established procedures and requirements.

In this position, you will apply strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and sound judgment to independently investigate and resolve a wide range of servicing requests. You will work across multiple systems and documentation sources to identify discrepancies, partner with internal business areas and plan administrators, and contribute to special projects and process improvement initiatives that strengthen controls and consistency across Plan Services.

• Research and resolve complex plan servicing requests involving participant, contract, transaction, and financial activity

• Review information across multiple systems and supporting documentation to identify discrepancies and determine appropriate resolution

• Perform financial and transactional research and reconciliations as needed

• Partner with internal business areas, plan administrators, and other stakeholders to resolve outstanding service issues

• Maintain complete and accurate documentation of research, findings, actions taken, and resolution

• Manage multiple requests and priorities while meeting established service expectations and deadlines

• Identify opportunities to improve processes, strengthen controls, reduce rework, and promote consistency across Plan Services

• Support operational initiatives, process improvements, and special projects as assigned

• Engage, as needed, in Plan Audit and Plan Reporting activities, including research, reconciliation, documentation, tracking, and responding to requests for plan-level information

• Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned based on business and operational needs

jobs.title: Technical Recruiter - New Grad
jobs.description:
Netic is the AI revenue engine for essential services who are the backbone of the American economy.  With $43M in funding from Founders Fund, Greylock, Hanabi, and Dylan Field who led our Series B, we helped our customers book hundreds of thousands of jobs across services industries in North America. There are now companies operating entirely AI-first on Netic.

 

You’ll join our team with relentless builders from Scale, Databricks, HRT, Meta, MIT, Stanford, and Harvard in bringing frontier AI to the physical economy, where the problems are hard, the data is complex, and the impact is immediate and tangible.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Netic is growing fast and tackling a massive, underserved market. This role is a rare opportunity for a highly ambitious recent graduate to break into the startup ecosystem and learn the art of recruiting from the ground up. You will work side-by-side with our founders, learn how top-tier engineering and go-to-market teams are built, and experience early-stage startup growth firsthand. If you want a fast-paced launchpad into recruiting, venture capital, or startup operations, this is the place to start.



WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Find and talk to the sharpest software engineers, PMs, and GTM leaders from top-tier universities and companies. You'll own the outreach strategy from day one.

 - Learn the full hiring lifecycle, which means everything from writing your own outbound pitches and running initial screens to managing the candidate pipeline and helping close offers.

 - Figure out ways to use AI and automation tools to handle the boring stuff so you can focus on writing better messages and talking to candidates.

 - Partner directly with our internal teams to calibrate on active roles and use data to spot and fix bottlenecks in our hiring process.

 - Give every single candidate an incredible experience and get really good at telling the Netic story.


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - A recent or upcoming degree from a top school, but more importantly, a habit of working hard and winning at things you care about (whether that’s academics, sports, or projects you built outside of class).

 - Real grit. We move fast and things change quickly here. You need to be comfortable with ambiguity and have a natural drive to run through walls to get things done.

 - Strong communication. You should love writing, speak clearly, and be confident holding your own in conversations with hyper-technical or highly experienced people.

 - An analytical mindset. Recruiting is a numbers game. You care about response rates, conversion loops, and using data to improve your process.

 - A high slope. You don’t need a background in recruiting, but you do need to learn technical concepts quickly, take feedback well, and adapt on the fly.

Our values

 1. Obsess over the customer

 2. Every second counts

 3. Sweat the details

 4. There are no blockers

 5. Be self-directed

 6. Seek and speak the truth

 7. Enjoy the ride

jobs.title: Analyst I, Falcon Complete GovCloud (Hybrid, St. Louis)
jobs.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

About the Role:

CrowdStrike Falcon® Complete GovCloud is looking for highly motivated, self-driven, technical analysts dedicated to making a difference in global security by protecting government organizations against the most advanced attackers in the world. Our Falcon Complete GovCloud virtual security operations center offers opportunities to expand your skill set through a wide variety of experiences, detecting and responding to incidents as they occur in real time for our government and public sector customers.

Analysts I operate exclusively within CrowdStrike's Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP)-authorized GovCloud environment, supporting customers with heightened compliance, data sovereignty, and security requirements. This is the entry point into the Falcon Complete GovCloud analyst career path. At this level, you will apply intermediate-level cybersecurity and technical skills across incident handling, alert triage, security monitoring, threat detection, digital forensics, incident response management, and malware analysis, while building the advanced communication, analytical thinking, and problem-solving capabilities that define the Falcon Complete GovCloud standard of service.

This position is open to candidates in St. Louis, MO.

Am I a Falcon Complete GovCloud Analyst I Candidate?

- Do you find yourself interested in putting your hands-on technical skills to the test in detecting, containing, and remediating incidents within U.S. government and public sector environments?

- Are you self-motivated and looking for an opportunity to rapidly accelerate your skills while working within one of the most compliance-driven and mission-critical cybersecurity environments in the industry?

- Do you crave new and innovative work that directly supports the security of government organizations and the missions they serve?

- Do you have an incident response or information security background that you are not fully utilizing, particularly experience in or exposure to government, Department of War (DoW, formerly the Department of Defense), or intelligence community environments?

- Are you capable of communicating technical findings clearly to both technical teams and government customer management?

- Do you love working around mission-driven, smart people who you can learn from and mentor on a daily basis?

What You'll Do:

- Execute alert triage across the Falcon Complete GovCloud environment at an intermediate proficiency level, developing complete triage strategies, managing multiple alert sources, implementing comprehensive investigation procedures, and developing detailed documentation, all within FedRAMP authorization boundaries and applicable federal compliance requirements.

- Operate the CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor within the GovCloud environment at an intermediate proficiency level, configuring sophisticated monitoring parameters across environments, analyzing security event patterns to identify potential threats, and adapting sensor capabilities to meet the varied security requirements of government and public sector customers.

- Implement and manage security monitoring and detection within the GovCloud environment at an intermediate proficiency level, developing complete monitoring solutions, implementing complex detection methods, managing multiple security tools, and developing custom detection rules.

- Apply threat detection capabilities within the GovCloud environment at an intermediate proficiency level, demonstrating growing independence in applying threat detection across familiar scenarios in support of government and public sector customer protection.

- Conduct digital forensics in support of customer incident response at an intermediate proficiency level, developing complete forensic strategies, managing multiple evidence sources, implementing comprehensive documentation frameworks, and developing detailed reports.

- Execute incident response management across the full incident lifecycle at an intermediate proficiency level, developing complete response strategies, implementing complex containment methods, managing evidence collection, and managing cross-team coordination, aligned to NIST SP 800-61 (Computer Security Incident Handling Guide) and applicable federal incident response frameworks.

- Perform malware analysis in support of customer incident response at an intermediate proficiency level, contributing effectively to malware analysis projects and offering practical suggestions to inform containment decisions and remediation planning.

- Operate the CrowdStrike Falcon platform user interface within the GovCloud environment at an intermediate proficiency level, performing investigations and triage, applying filters, generating reports, and using threat graphs to support incident response workflows for government and public sector customers.

- Apply intermediate-level technical troubleshooting within the GovCloud environment, handling complex technical issues independently, performing thorough root cause analysis, identifying patterns in recurring issues, and implementing preventive measures to reduce recurrence.

- Apply intermediate-level Linux administration knowledge within the GovCloud environment, managing complex Linux environments independently, implementing advanced system configurations, implementing automation through shell scripting, and maintaining security hardening standards.

- Apply intermediate-level Windows systems administration knowledge within the GovCloud environment, managing complex Active Directory structures independently, implementing and maintaining Windows security features and compliance requirements, and troubleshooting complex system issues.

- Communicate effectively with government and public sector customer management and internal stakeholders at an advanced proficiency level, communicating complex ideas with exceptional clarity and authority, anticipating the needs and motivations of others, and adapting messaging to guide conversations toward desired outcomes.

- Deliver high-quality presentations of technical findings and recommendations at an advanced proficiency level, presenting complex or high-stakes topics with clarity, authority, and persuasion, and adjusting in real time based on audience cues and feedback.

- Apply advanced problem-solving to GovCloud operational challenges, developing innovative solutions to complex problems, anticipating problems before they arise, and evaluating long-term impacts and broader implications of solutions.

- Manage time and workload effectively across concurrent incident response assignments at an intermediate proficiency level, demonstrating confidence in prioritization and adjusting approach based on context and operational feedback.

- Contribute to CrowdStrike's industry thought leadership through blog posts, CrowdCasts, and other public-facing engagements, representing the Falcon Complete GovCloud team's expertise and mission focus.

What You'll Need:

Successful candidates will have experience in one or more of the following areas:

- Incident Handling: Experience conducting or managing incident response for organizations, investigating targeted threats including Advanced Persistent Threats (APT), Organized Crime, and Hacktivists, with preference for experience in or supporting government, DoW, or public sector environments. Demonstrated intermediate-level ability to develop complete triage strategies, implement complex analysis methods, and manage multiple alert sources independently.

- Computer Forensic Analysis: A background using a variety of forensic analysis tools in incident response investigations to determine the extent and scope of compromise. Intermediate-level ability to develop complete forensic strategies, implement complex analysis methods, manage multiple evidence sources, and produce detailed investigation reports within regulated or compliance-driven environments.

- Systems Administration: Intermediate-level understanding of system internals across Windows, Mac, and Linux platforms, including the ability to manage complex configurations, implement automation through scripting, handle complex troubleshooting scenarios, and maintain security hardening standards sufficient to execute countermeasures and remediation within a managed services context.

- Security Monitoring and Detection: Intermediate-level capability to develop complete monitoring solutions, implement complex detection methods, create effective alert workflows, manage multiple security tools, optimize detection accuracy, and develop custom detection rules within a security operations context.

- Network Forensic Analysis: Knowledge of network protocols and network analysis tools, with the ability to perform analysis of associated network logs to support incident scoping and attribution within the GovCloud environment.

- Malware Analysis: Intermediate-level ability to contribute effectively to malware analysis projects, applying static and dynamic techniques to understand the nature, behavior, and intent of malicious code encountered in customer environments.

- Incident Remediation: Understanding of targeted attack lifecycles with the ability to develop customized tactical and strategic remediation plans for compromised organizations, including those operating under federal compliance mandates.

- Network Operations and Architecture/Engineering: Understanding of secure network architecture and network operations, including familiarity with federal network security standards applicable to GovCloud environments.

- Programming/Scripting: Experience coding in one or more of the following: C, C#, VB, Python, Perl, Ruby on Rails, and .NET, applied to automation, tooling, or analysis support within a security operations context.

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Additional Qualifications:

All candidates must also demonstrate the following:

- Advanced analytical thinking capability, with demonstrated ability to optimize performance by redesigning or elevating analytical practices to improve incident response outcomes for government and public sector customers.

- Advanced communication capability, with demonstrated ability to communicate complex ideas with exceptional clarity and authority, anticipating the needs and motivations of others and adapting messaging accordingly.

- Advanced presentation capability, with demonstrated ability to present complex or high-stakes topics with clarity, authority, and persuasion to government and public sector customer management and internal stakeholders.

- Advanced problem-solving capability, with demonstrated ability to develop innovative solutions to complex problems, anticipate issues before they arise, and evaluate long-term impacts of solutions.

- Intermediate-level time management capability, with demonstrated confidence in prioritizing tasks, managing workload, and meeting deadlines while maintaining quality under pressure.

- Demonstrated desire to grow and expand both technical and soft skills, with a commitment to continuous professional development in the federal cybersecurity space.

- Strong organizational skills sufficient to manage concurrent incident response workstreams.

- Ability to foster a positive, collaborative work environment and maintain a professional attitude under pressure.

Education:

A Bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Mathematics, Information Security, Information Assurance, Information Security Management, Intelligence Studies, Cybersecurity, Cybersecurity Policy, or a related field is preferred. Applicants without a degree but with relevant work experience, military service, and/or industry training and certifications will be considered.

Creative Artists Agency (CAA) is the leading entertainment and sports agency, with global expertise in filmed and live entertainment, digital media, publishing, sponsorship sales and endorsements, licensing, media finance, consumer investing, fashion, trademark licensing, and philanthropy. Distinguished by its culture of collaboration and exceptional client service, CAA’s diverse workforce identifies, innovates, and amplifies opportunities for the people and organizations that shape culture and inspire the world. The trailblazer of the agency business, CAA was the first to build a sports business, create an investment bank, launch a venture fund, found technology start-up companies, establish a philanthropic arm, build a business in China, and form a brand marketing services division, among other innovations.

Position Summary:

CAA is seeking a Junior Analyst to support a Contract Administration Executive in the Books and Publishing department. The position is part of a small team that works to ensure accuracy in Publisher reporting of sales and royalty earnings on behalf of clients and Agent colleagues and to use this same reporting for insights into project performance and trend analysis.

jobs.title: Quantitative Financial Analyst I
jobs.description:
- Job Summary: The Quantitative Developer builds, tests, and maintains the financial models, calculation libraries, and data pipelines that power Clearwater’s analytics. This is an early-career opening intended for candidates completing a master’s program in a quantitative field. Quantitative Developers learn Clearwater’s financial models and data model, implement calculations as tested and reviewed code alongside software engineering teams, and grow into ownership of a domain over time. The role blends applied quantitative finance with hands-on software development, and no prior professional experience is required — we expect strong programming fundamentals and a solid quantitative foundation, and will teach the rest. Responsibilities:

- Assist senior Quantitative Developers and Quantitative Financial Analysts in researching and implementing new calculations as part of larger projects.

- Write clear, tested Python that follows team standards, and contribute to the shared libraries and internal tooling used across the team through the normal code review process.

- Accurately replicate existing mathematical models in Excel and Python, including client analytics tie-outs.

- Perform acceptance, regression, and integration testing of financial models using the existing automated testing frameworks.

- Write, read, and edit SQL queries to extract security, position, and market data for model inputs, validation, and ad-hoc analysis.

- Implement numerical and statistical methods — Monte Carlo simulation, solvers and root-finding, interpolation — under the direction of more senior team members.

- Build and maintain components of the data pipelines that source, normalize, and validate data consumed by financial models.

- Research and learn the data model for your domain, including the data consumed and produced by the code base.

- Assist operations teams in understanding how data inputs impact calculations, and assist developers in analyzing unexpected regressions for a code change.

- Identify and build small automations, including the effective use of AI-assisted development tools, to simplify recurring analytical, validation, and documentation work.

- Proactively update internal documentation to reflect new features and calculation methodology.

Cenovus is an integrated energy company headquartered in Calgary. We’re committed to maximizing value by developing our assets in a safe, responsible and cost-efficient manner. Our operations include oil sands projects in northern Alberta, thermal and conventional crude oil and natural gas projects across Western Canada, crude oil production offshore Newfoundland and Labrador and natural gas and liquids production offshore China and Indonesia. New Grad Program

We all want to start our careers on the right foot, and Cenovus Energy’s New Grad Program helps you do exactly that. Through three, 12-month rotations in your chosen discipline, you’ll get access to real-world projects, cutting-edge technology, and mentorship from industry experts.

What we offer:

- Total rewards: Competitive salary, performance-based bonus, vacation time and pension contributions to support your financial future.

- Networking & events: Attend career development sessions, build your professional network and engage in volunteer work.

- New Grad committee: Enjoy fun and inclusive events that help build community and foster connections across the organization.

The Cenovus experience

We foster a culture of continuous learning and development to support employees as they build meaningful careers. We offer a variety of employee development initiatives, including:

- Internal course offerings

- Education assistance for additional development

- Opportunities to work on special projects

- Leadership development programs for emerging and established leaders

We actively promote internal job movement, recognizing the value of gaining new perspectives, building connections across teams, and applying expertise in new ways.
